objective_text: Plot complex numbers on Argand diagram

questions.stem: Plot the complex number -3 + 4i on the Argand diagram.
questions.solution: The complex number is in the form of a + bi. The real part (-3) corresponds to the x-coordinate and the imaginary part (4) corresponds to the y-coordinate on the Argand diagram. So, the correct plot is at the point [-3, 4].
questions.explanation: An Argand diagram plots complex numbers as points in the Cartesian plane, with the real part on the horizontal axis and the imaginary part on the vertical axis.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to mix up the real and imaginary parts. Remember that -3 is the x-coordinate and 4 is the y-coordinate.

questions.stem: Find the coordinates of the point representing the complex number 5 - 6i on the Argand diagram.
questions.solution: The complex number is in the form of a + bi. The real part (5) corresponds to the x-coordinate and the imaginary part (-6) corresponds to the y-coordinate on the Argand diagram. So, the correct coordinates are [5, -6].
questions.explanation: In an Argand diagram, the real part determines the horizontal position and the imaginary part determines the vertical position.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to reverse the signs of the real and imaginary parts. Ensure that you plot the correct sign for each component.

questions.stem: Plot the complex number 2i on the Argand diagram.
questions.solution: The complex number is in the form of a + bi. Since there is no real part (a = 0), the point will be on the imaginary axis. The imaginary part (b = 2) determines the y-coordinate. So, the correct plot is at [0, 2].
questions.explanation: When the real part is zero, the complex number lies solely on the imaginary axis.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to assume that the point would be at [2, 0], but remember that when there's no real part, the x-coordinate should be zero.

questions.stem: Find the coordinates of the point representing the complex number -4 + 0i on the Argand diagram.
questions.solution: The complex number is in the form of a + bi. The real part (-4) corresponds to the x-coordinate and the imaginary part (0) means it lies on the horizontal axis. So, the correct coordinates are [-4, 0].
questions.explanation: When the imaginary part is zero, the complex number lies solely on the real axis.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to assume that the point would be at [0, -4], but remember that when there's no imaginary part, the y-coordinate should be zero.

questions.stem: Plot the complex number 3 + 3i on the Argand diagram.
questions.solution: The complex number is in the form of a + bi. The real part (3) corresponds to the x-coordinate and the imaginary part (3) corresponds to the y-coordinate on the Argand diagram. So, the correct plot is at [3, 3].
questions.explanation: In this case, both the real and imaginary parts are equal, resulting in a point that lies along the line y = x.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to mix up the signs of the coordinates. Ensure that you plot the correct values for each component.

questions.stem: Find the coordinates of the point representing the complex number -2 - 3i on the Argand diagram.
questions.solution: The complex number is in the form of a + bi. The real part (-2) corresponds to the x-coordinate and the imaginary part (-3) corresponds to the y-coordinate on the Argand diagram. So, the correct coordinates are [-2, -3].
questions.explanation: When both parts have negative signs, they represent a point in the third quadrant of the Argand diagram.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget the negative sign for one or both components. Remember that both the real and imaginary parts should retain their signs.

questions.stem: Plot the complex number -1 + √3i on the Argand diagram.
questions.solution: The complex number is in the form of a + bi. The real part (-1) corresponds to the x-coordinate and the imaginary part (√3) corresponds to the y-coordinate on the Argand diagram. So, the correct plot is at [-1, √3].
questions.explanation: When plotting irrational numbers like √3i, it's important to retain the exact form.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to try to simplify √3i or convert it to a decimal. In this case, it should be plotted as is.
